CCQ-1992); federal and provincial commercial/AML statutes are bilingual (English/French) and apply concurrently.

Agreement between Canada and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force 6 September 2016

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CCQ), arts. 2236-2265 (société en commandite / limited partnership), in particular arts. 2236, 2242, and 2246; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 9-31 (registration) and ss. 34-39 (declaration contents).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Limited partners' contributions are fixed contractually in the partnership agreement (CCQ art. 2246) and may be in money, credit, or property. No escrow account or bank attestation is required by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the partnership agreement (convention de société) proposed to this meeting be adopted and ratified in full; FURTHER RESOLVED, that each partner's capital contribution be subscribed as set out in Schedule A and credited to the partnership's capital accounts; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the partnership's registered office be established at [address in Québec] and that [Authorized Representative] be appointed to receive notice and to act as agent before the Registraire des entreprises; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Representative Name] be appointed operations manager of the general partner, with authority to open bank and merchant payment accounts (Stripe, PayPal), to execute vendor and customer agreements, and to obtain all municipal permits required for the automated dropshipping business; and that all acts already performed in furtherance hereof be ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name check service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the central enterprise register online to confirm that the proposed name is distinctive, lawful, and not confusing with existing legal persons or partnerships. The name must include the designation 'Société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' Where the Registrar's automated notice indicates possible conflict, file a name clearance request and await a written opinion before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Proposed name with mandatory designation 'Société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'
Identification of the general partner
Description of the partnership's principal object
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an alternative name or file written representations with the Registrar within 15 days; a revised declaration may be refiled without additional penalty in the same service session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement (convention de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties (general and limited partners), optionally assisted by a notary of the Chambre des notaires du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written partnership agreement setting out each limited partner's capital contribution, the general partner's exclusive management powers, profit and loss allocation, restrictions on limited partner participation, withdrawal and dissolution terms, and the address of the registered establishment in Québec. A notarized deed is required if an immovable is contributed.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (or authenticated extract for filing purposes)
Schedule of capital contributions
Proof of identity and legal capacity of each partner
Power of attorney if the agreement is signed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the extent of the general partner's powers, amend the partnership agreement by written modification and file a corrected extract with the declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration (immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (online portal 'Mon espace' or counter service in Québec City / Montréal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Déclaration d'immatriculation identifying the partnership's name, object, establishment address in Québec, and the name and domicile of the general partner(s). Pay the prescribed duty (CAD 38 electronic / CAD 60 paper, approx. USD 28/44). Upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and a certificate of registration and transmits the registration to Revenu Québec and federal authorities.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration (LPE-1)
Partnership agreement or authenticated extract
Identification documents of the general partner
Proof of address of the establishment in Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is incomplete or refused, file an amending declaration within 30 days; administrative review by the Registrar or judicial remedy before the Court of Québec is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec, in coordination with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership for GST/QST accounts using the NEQ; the CRA will coordinate issuance of a federal Business Number (BN) where required. Payroll accounts with Revenu Québec and CNESST are required only upon hiring staff. The partnership is a pass-through reporting entity that must file annual information returns (TP-600 / T5013).
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate
Partnership agreement
Identification of the general partner and non-resident status, if any
Contact details of the partnership's designated representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact Revenu Québec business client services directly; if a filing deadline is missed, apply for voluntary disclosure before any audit to reduce penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking, payment processor onboarding, and municipal permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank or financial institution of choice; local municipality of the establishment's address; Stripe/PayPal onboarding teams
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Canadian-dollar business bank account in the partnership's name using the NEQ and the partnership agreement; complete KYC and beneficial ownership statements. Onboard Stripe and PayPal with the registered entity details, annual revenue projections, and a merchant compliance / refund policy. Confirm with the local municipality whether a home-based business permit (permis d'exploitation) is required; no provincial retail licence is required for ISIC 4791 in Québec.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration (NEQ)
Partnership agreement
Identification of signatories and beneficial owners
Proof of address and bank account authorization
Merchant compliance policy documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment processor requests enhanced due diligence, provide an organizational chart, transaction flow narrative, and supplier list; if a municipal permit is refused, apply to the municipal inspection committee or obtain a variance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable at formation; the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) and municipal permit offices are only relevant if warehousing or physical premises are later leased.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for pure e-commerce / automated dropshipping under ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110; a municipal 'permis d'exploitation' (business permit) may be required depending on the location of the registered establishment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment is required for an enterprise with no physical production facilities; no REAFIE registration is triggered for pure dropshipping operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure dropshipping operations; if warehousing is later established, the operator must comply with the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2), municipal wastewater by-laws and waste-handling requirements. No VOC thresholds apply as no manufacturing or assembly occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a home office or leased commercial office: obtain a fire safety certificate (attestation de sécurité incendie) from the local fire safety service and confirm that the building's occupancy certificate permits office use. Upon the first hire, register with the CNESST for occupational health and safety and post the mandatory workplace safety notice.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada – Business Registration Online and My Business Account portal; provincial counterpart: Revenu Québec – Mon dossier d'entreprise portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Canadian Limited Partnership, register through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) using Form RC1 or the online application to obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and required program accounts (GST/HST 'RT', import/export 'RM', payroll 'RP'). A foreign entity without a Canadian presence must follow the CRA non-resident registration procedure, designate a representative for service, and evidence the partnership's commercial activity in Canada. For Quebec, register separately with Revenu Québec via the enterprise online service to obtain a QST registration number if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, and file provincial registration amendments. Statutory forms: RC1 (federal) and LM-1/LM-2 (Quebec).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible – The LP is fiscally transparent under federal Income Tax Act s. 96 and the Quebec Taxation Act; income and losses flow through to partners. For GST/HST and QST purposes, the partnership is separately registered as a person under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act and the QST Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box election; foreign entity classification is governed by CRA Folio S4-F1-C1. A Canadian LP may use Elections under the Excise Tax Act s. 156 to treat closely related persons as one person for GST/HST, and similar provincial elections may be available under the QST Act. Canada's hybrid mismatch rules under ITA s. 94.2 apply to prevent unintended double non-taxation; no elective classification mechanism exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) administered federally, and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administered by Revenu Québec under the QST Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies during any calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold) for GST/HST; QST registration follows the same CAD 30,000 threshold for commercial activities carried on in Quebec. Non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies to Canadian customers must register once the threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime exists in Canada or Quebec. Electronic invoices are accepted as authentic records if generated and retained in accordance with CRA GST/HST Memorandum 15.1 and Quebec's record-keeping standards. GST/HST returns are filed via GST/HST NETFILE (GST34 procedure); Revenu Québec requires electronic filing through its secure online services. No API-based fiscal clearance is mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI permits 0% GST/HST and QST for supplies of goods that are exported by the registrant from Canada to a destination outside Canada as part of a supply to a non-resident; direct drop-shipping of goods from Canada to a foreign destination per the non-resident purchaser's instructions; and services performed for a non-resident not connected to Canadian real property or tangible personal property in Canada. The registrant must retain commercial invoices, export shipping documents, and evidence of foreign destination; failure to substantiate zero-rating results in reassessment and penalties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A electronic CAED or equivalent CBSA-validated export declaration)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing physical export shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Repatriation Proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years of the reporting period, extended indefinitely for misrepresentation. False zero-rating claims attract penalties under ETA ss. 280, 285, and ITA ss. 163.2 (5% to 10% of net tax adjustment plus daily interest, and up to 50% gross negligence penalties). Quebec levies parallel administrative penalties under the QST Act and the Taxation Act. Criminal tax evasion is punishable under ITA s. 239(1) with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment; partners may be jointly liable for false statements on partnership returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Foreign-exchange reporting, anti-money-laundering, and payment-service controls also involve the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada, the Canada Revenue Agency, the Canada Border Services Agency, and the Department of Finance Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has a freely convertible Canadian dollar with no general exchange controls, capital controls, or mandatory repatriation regime. Current-account receipts, investment capital, dividends, partnership distributions, loan proceeds, and trade payments may generally be converted and transferred through Canadian financial institutions, subject to bank compliance, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering requirements, tax compliance, contractual restrictions, and adequate source-of-funds evidence. A Quebec limited partnership should document its partnership agreement, general partner authority, beneficial ownership, tax residence, contribution records, and distribution approvals. Distributions to non-resident partners may create Canadian withholding-tax, information-reporting, treaty, and non-resident filing obligations. Payments to related non-residents must also be reviewed for transfer-pricing, thin-capitalization, shareholder-benefit, and withholding-tax consequences. There is no general legal requirement to obtain prior foreign-exchange approval for capital contributions or profit remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or general deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts into Canadian dollars. Export proceeds may remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the account holder's discretion. The business must retain commercial, customs, payment, and accounting records and comply with applicable income-tax, GST/HST, Quebec sales-tax, customs, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering requirements. Cross-border payments may be reported by financial institutions under applicable anti-money-laundering and international tax-reporting rules. Foreign-currency transactions should be recorded using a consistently applied accounting exchange-rate policy, with realized and unrealized exchange differences appropriately recognized.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection and foreign-currency settlement, subject to provider eligibility, Canadian residency and business-verification rules, permitted-use restrictions, and transaction-volume limits. Stripe and PayPal may support Canadian businesses but do not replace a full-service Canadian bank account and may impose rolling reserves, delayed settlement, chargeback reserves, prohibited-business restrictions, and enhanced review for automated dropshipping. An offshore electronic-money institution cannot assume unrestricted access to Canadian payment services. A provider carrying on retail payment activities in Canada may need registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act and must satisfy applicable operational-risk, safeguarding, funds-handling, sanctions, consumer-protection, and anti-money-laundering requirements. Client funds must not be represented as deposit-insured Canadian bank deposits unless legally eligible. Offshore settlement accounts should be supported by contracts, invoices, processor statements, beneficial-ownership evidence, and a documented funds-flow map.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory requirement for all directors or partners to attend a branch in person. Remote onboarding may be available for eligible Canadian entities, but bank policy controls the result. For a Quebec limited partnership, the bank will ordinarily identify and verify the general partner, authorized signing officers, limited partners meeting applicable ownership or control thresholds, and ultimate beneficial owners. In-person attendance, notarized or certified documents, video interviews, Canadian address verification, or a branch appointment may be required where the entity is newly formed, foreign-controlled, lacks Canadian operating history, uses high-risk jurisdictions, has a complex ownership chain, or proposes high-volume cross-border payments. A limited partnership may not have directors; the bank should receive equivalent authority evidence for the general partner and designated account signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: New Quebec limited partnership with no Canadian banking or trading history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of constitution or registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; executed limited-partnership agreement; general-partner certificate; partnership register; ownership and control chart; tax-account confirmations where available; business plan; expected transaction profile; opening balance and capital-contribution evidence; and board, partner, or general-partner resolutions authorizing the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership, foreign general partner, or opaque multi-tier ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for every relevant entity; complete ownership chain to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and residential-address evidence; tax-residency information; incumbency or good-standing certificates; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; intercompany agreements; and an explanation of commercial rationale for the Canadian structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automated dropshipping model with third-party suppliers and customer payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier contracts; customer terms; website and product catalogue; fulfilment and shipping workflow; sample purchase orders and invoices; processor agreements; chargeback and refund policy; customs and import documentation; product-compliance screening; prohibited-goods controls; expected monthly volumes; average ticket size; countries served; and a written description separating customer receipts, supplier payments, taxes, refunds, and partner distributions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High payment-processor exposure, rapid volume growth, or elevated chargeback risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical processor statements; chargeback ratios; reserve arrangements; fraud-monitoring procedures; customer-verification controls; delivery-confirmation data; refund records; customer-service procedures; insurance evidence where relevant; and a liquidity buffer sufficient to cover processor holds, refunds, taxes, and supplier obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent wires involving multiple jurisdictions or unrelated counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty master file; invoices; purchase orders; bills of lading or delivery confirmations; customs records; contract-to-payment reconciliation; sanctions-screening results; payment-purpose descriptions; beneficial-owner information for material counterparties; and a documented approval matrix for outbound payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore EMI, virtual-asset platform, money-services business, or payment intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licence or registration evidence; regulatory perimeter analysis; account ownership confirmation; safeguarding description; service agreement; transaction statements; source-of-funds evidence; sanctions and AML policy; reconciliation reports; and a written explanation of why the provider is necessary and how funds return to the Canadian operating account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cash activity, third-party deposits, or payments inconsistent with the stated business model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cashless treasury policy; prohibition on third-party funding unless contractually justified; customer and supplier verification procedures; expected-payment matrix; exception-approval records; and monthly reconciliation demonstrating that account activity matches the approved business profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large capital contribution or partner distribution to a non-resident
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed contribution or distribution resolution; partnership-accounting ledger; partner capital accounts; source-of-funds evidence; tax advice on withholding and reporting; treaty-residency certificates where relevant; remittance calculation; and evidence that the payment is not an undisclosed loan, dividend substitution, or prohibited third-party transfer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital contributions through a Canadian bank account held in the exact legal name of the Quebec limited partnership. Use a regulated correspondent-bank wire with the partnership's legal name, account number, transit and institution numbers, SWIFT/BIC where applicable, and a precise payment narrative such as 'capital contribution under limited-partnership agreement' or 'partner loan under executed loan agreement.' Canada has no universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system; the bank may nevertheless request an internal purpose classification and supporting documents. Before receipt, provide the partnership agreement, contribution or loan instrument, remitter ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner details, and expected amount and currency. Reconcile the incoming wire to the partnership ledger and retain bank confirmations. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated entities, payment processors, or unidentified third parties. For foreign affiliates, assess Canadian thin-capitalization, transfer-pricing, withholding-tax, interest-deductibility, shareholder-loan, and partnership-allocation consequences.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian bank wires, correspondent-bank transfers, or commercial letters of credit for supplier and logistics payments. A SWIFT MT103 or its current equivalent may be used for a customer-credit transfer, subject to the sending and receiving banks' message standards; it is not itself proof of an underlying trade transaction. Attach or retain the commercial invoice, purchase order, supplier contract, shipping evidence, customs information, sanctions-screening result, and payment-purpose record. Use a commercial documentary letter of credit where supplier performance, documentary control, or counterparty risk justifies it; define required documents, Incoterms, inspection terms, discrepancy rules, insurance, currency, expiry, and bank charges. For ordinary dropshipping, require payments to match verified suppliers and invoices, and maintain controls over refunds, chargebacks, returns, duties, GST/HST, Quebec sales tax, and foreign withholding obligations. Maintain dual authorization and transaction-level reconciliation between the bank, accounting system, payment processor, and inventory or fulfilment records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, documented under applicable master trading terms and supported by an identifiable forecast or committed exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are not freely deliverable or where settlement is contractually cash-settled, subject to dealer eligibility, counterparty documentation, margin or collateral terms, and applicable derivatives rules.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term currency liquidity management, subject to documented maturity, settlement, counterparty, and credit-limit controls.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps where the partnership has a genuine currency and interest-rate exposure and the transaction is approved under a written treasury policy.

Currency options, collars, and option-based hedges where permitted by the dealer and suitable for the entity's risk profile, with documented premium, liquidity, valuation, accounting, and break-cost controls.

Operational controls: hedge only identifiable commercial or financing exposures; prohibit speculative trading; establish counterparty limits; obtain appropriate ISDA or dealer documentation; maintain confirmations and valuations; monitor collateral and termination exposure; obtain tax and accounting treatment advice; and ensure the general partner has expressly authorized derivatives activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) for the Quebec limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the limited partnership's fiscal year-end; conflicts with a calendar-year end therefore require filing no later than early March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties accrue on a daily basis under Quebec's Legal Publicity Act; repeated non-filing causes the registrar to issue an administrative notice and may lead to cancellation of the enterprise registration, loss of limited partnership status, and inability to enforce juridical acts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and partnership financial statement information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than five months after the partnership fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the return is due by May 31 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file T5013 on time may result in late filing penalties per partner, daily penalties in egregious cases, and the CRA can impose monetary penalties and require information returns even after administrative enforcement procedures are initiated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) return for the e-commerce/dropshipping activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an annual filer, generally due no later than three months after the end of the reporting period; a December 31 fiscal year-end creates a March 31 filing deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid net tax accrues daily compound interest and penalties for late remittance; failure by a GST/HST and QST registrant to file may trigger directive assessments, garnishments, and revocation of registration privileges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update of registrable information when a partner or general partner changes during the annual cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 60 days after the event or, if no event occurs, covered by the annual declaration due within 60 days after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration of a partner change can attract late fees; the registrar may reject filings until required annual declaration and penalty are paid, and continued non-compliance can result in administrative strike-off of the LP's registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership solely by reason of its status as an LP. A mandatory audit may arise under the partnership agreement, from binding bank or investor covenants, or if the LP is a reporting issuer or otherwise required by a Canadian financial regulator. For routine dropshipping operations, no provincial compulsory audit threshold applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the default for a private Quebec LP; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is required only if the entity is publicly accountable or if the partnership agreement explicitly mandates IFRS. Tax allocations and partner capital accounts are tracked on a fiscal basis consistent with the CRA and Revenu Québec filing rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not operate a public beneficial-ownership register for limited partnerships. The annual declaration to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec must accurately identify all general partners and the place of management; limited partners are not disclosed in the public registry. For anti-money-laundering purposes under FINTRAC, the LP must maintain current beneficial-ownership records of every partner and update them whenever there is a transfer of partnership interest, including automatic dropshipping ownership restructures.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (capital contributions, distributions, and transfers of interests)
Register of General Partner Resolutions and Management Minute Book
Register of Partnership Agreement, Declarations, and Amendments filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – USD 400 depending on Quebec registered agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 7,500 for a small private LP when an audit is contractually or regulatorily required; not a routine expense for an exempt private dropshipping LP

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
